MIC.P.4.1-5.text: The Mountain of the House of the LORD

MIC.1.1-1.text: The LORD gives Micah a message about Samaria and Jerusalem

MIC.1.2-4.text: The LORD comes down and the mountains melt like wax

MIC.1.5-5.text: Jacob’s sin is seen in Samaria and Jerusalem

MIC.1.6-7.text: The LORD will destroy Samaria and its idols

MIC.1.8-10.text: Micah mourns because Samaria’s wound has reached Judah

MIC.1.11-12.text: Disaster from the LORD reaches the towns near Jerusalem

MIC.1.13-14.text: Micah speaks against Lachish and Moresheth-gath

MIC.1.15-16.text: Micah tells the people of Judah to mourn for exile

MIC.2.1-2.text: Woe to people who plan evil and take fields and houses

MIC.2.3-5.text: The LORD plans disaster for the proud oppressors

MIC.2.6-8.text: God accuses his people of acting like enemies

MIC.2.9-11.text: God accuses oppressors of driving out women and children

MIC.3.1-3.text: Micah accuses Israel’s leaders of harming the people

MIC.3.4-4.text: The LORD will not answer the leaders’ cry

MIC.3.5-7.text: God will bring darkness on prophets who lead people astray

MIC.3.8-8.text: Micah is filled with power to speak about Israel’s sin

MIC.3.9-11.text: Leaders, priests and prophets act wrongly for money

MIC.3.12-12.text: Jerusalem will become a heap of rubble

MIC.4.1-1.text: In the last days the LORD’s mountain will be highest

MIC.4.2-3.text: Nations will learn God’s ways and live in peace

MIC.4.4-5.text: God’s people will live safely and follow the LORD forever

MIC.4.6-8.text: The LORD will gather the outcast and rule in Zion

MIC.4.9-10.text: Zion will go to Babylon, and the LORD will rescue her

MIC.4.11-12.text: Many nations gather against Zion, but God has a plan

MIC.4.13-13.text: Zion will break many peoples and give wealth to the LORD

MIC.5.1-1.text: Enemies attack Jerusalem and strike Israel’s judge

MIC.5.2-3.text: A ruler from long ago will come from small Bethlehem

MIC.5.4-5.text: The ruler will shepherd Israel and bring peace

MIC.5.6-6.text: The ruler will deliver Israel from Assyria

MIC.5.7-7.text: Jacob’s remnant will be like dew from the LORD

MIC.5.8-9.text: Jacob’s remnant will be like a strong lion

MIC.5.10-11.text: The LORD will destroy Israel’s horses, chariots and cities

MIC.5.12-15.text: The LORD will remove sorcery and idols from Israel

MIC.6.1-2.text: The LORD calls the mountains to hear his case against Israel

MIC.6.3-5.text: The LORD reminds Israel how he saved the people

MIC.6.6-8.text: God wants people to act justly, love mercy and walk humbly

MIC.6.9-10.text: The LORD speaks against dishonest gain in the city

MIC.6.11-12.text: The LORD condemns false weights, violence and lies

MIC.6.13-15.text: Because of sin, Israel will not enjoy its harvest

MIC.6.16-16.text: Israel followed Ahab’s ways, so it will become a ruin

MIC.7.1-2.text: Micah grieves that no godly person is left

MIC.7.3-4.text: Leaders are corrupt, and the day of punishment has come

MIC.7.5-6.text: Micah says people cannot trust even family and friends

MIC.7.7-8.text: Micah will wait for God, who will be his light

MIC.7.9-9.text: Israel bears God’s anger until he brings justice

MIC.7.10-10.text: Israel’s enemy will be shamed and trampled

MIC.7.11-13.text: Israel’s walls will be rebuilt and people will return

MIC.7.14-15.text: Micah asks God to shepherd his people and show wonders

MIC.7.16-17.text: Nations will be ashamed and tremble before the LORD

MIC.7.18-18.text: Micah praises God for pardoning sin and showing love

MIC.7.19-20.text: God will forgive Israel’s sins and keep his promises
